samuel1.29.p1.b1.text: Now the Philistines brought all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.

samuel1.29.p1.b2.text: As the Philistine leaders marched out their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men marched behind them with Achish.

samuel1.29.p1.b4.text: Is this not David, the servant of King Saul of Israel?…from the day he defected until today I have found no fault in him.

samuel1.29.p2.b1.text: Send that man back and let him return to the place you assigned him. He must not go down with us into battle only to become our adversary during the war.

samuel1.29.p2.b2.text: What better way for him to regain the favor of his master than with the heads of our men?

samuel1.29.p2.b3.text: Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands…

samuel1.29.p2.b4.text: …Is this not the David about whom they sing in their dances

samuel1.29.p3.b1.text: As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright in my sight…But you have no favor in the sight of the leaders.

samuel1.29.p3.b2.text: Therefore turn back now and go in peace, so that you will not do anything to displease the leaders of the Philistines.

samuel1.29.p3.b3.text: But what have I done?…What have you found against your servant, from the day I came to you until today, to keep me from going along to fight against the enemies of my lord the king?

samuel1.29.p4.b1.text: I know that you are as pleasing in my sight as an angel of God…

samuel1.29.p4.b2.text: Now then, get up early in the morning, along with your master’s servants who came with you, and go as soon as it is light.

samuel1.29.p4.b3.text: So David and his men got up early in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
